text:
marin: Following up on the onboarding RFC. TL;DR: prebench/deepbench storms are destabilizing runtime caches. I want to prototype a two-layer pacing approach: (1) intake admission shim that enforces an overall probe budget, (2) prober-local backpressure that protects KV and prioritizes golden inputs.

alex: makes sense. Do you have specific signals in mind for the intake shim? ingest qps? token-weighted RPS?

marin: both. The intake shim should compute a cost score per model = ingest_qps * expected_token_cost. We then convert to a soft probe allowance. Important: soft == best-effort with priority weights, not a hard failure.

lia: can we avoid changing correctness gating? anything that affects pass/fail of tokenizer/parity checks is a no-go. Performance gating only.

sam: agree with lia. Also we should record the effective probe schedule with every model artifact so any downstream evals know what was actually sampled.

marin: rough config example (toy):
```json
{
  "pacing": {
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "intake": {
      "global_probe_budget_rps": "200",
      "cost_function": "ingest_qps * token_cost",
      "priority_weights": {"critical": 2.0, "standard": 1.0, "low": 0.5}
    },
    "prober": {
      "golden_watermark": "0.75",
      "min_golden_first": true,
      "kv_safe_threshold": "0.65",
      "evict_policy": "prefer-oldest-non-golden"
    },
    "telemetry": {
      "emit_effective_probe_plan": true,
      "metrics": ["onboard_latency_ms","golden_coverage","kv_miss_rate"]
    }
  }
}
```

ops_lead: if the model is targeted to a dedicated pool, intake shim must respect capacity reservations. we should have an override flag: `deployment_hint: dedicated_override` to bypass global budget.

alex: runtime concern: KV poisoning from many prefixes. prober should cap unique-prefixes in-flight and favor golden prefixes first. also TTL-based eviction for stale prefixes.

marin: good call. propose that prober maintains two prefix LRU buckets: golden and others. when kv_util > kv_safe_threshold, evict from "others" bucket oldest-first.

sam: simulation is mandatory. i can build a synthetic ingest trace with mixed priorities and seqlen distributions. what are success criteria?

lia: define success as: golden_coverage >= 0.8 for at least 90% of models within first 30 minutes; kv_miss_rate under 5% system-wide; onboarding tail latency P99 reduced by 30% vs baseline.

marin: love those targets. sam, can you also simulate a "rush" scenario with 200 models landing within 10 minutes? we need to know if low-priority models starve.

sam: yes. i'll produce two traces: steady-state and rush. will output dashboards for the three metrics.

devops-bot: alert: prebench-scheduler deployed probe throttle v0.1 -> intake shim enabled in staging.

ops_lead: run the staging sim and share results in this thread. if staging looks sane, we can RFC for rollout plan and fallback behaviors.

marin: action items: marin will draft RFC with exact cost formula + config schema; sam will deliver ingest traces and sim dashboards; alex will prototype prober eviction buckets; lia will write acceptance criteria for deterministic checks. target: RFC up by Friday.

alex: small UX note: expose the effective_probe_plan in model registry UI so SREs can inspect recent onboarding behavior.

marin: agreed. thanks all. if anyone wants to add constraints (eg: per-customer fairness or API rate interplay) drop comments here.

sam: acked, starting the trace generator now.

lia: +1, will draft the deterministic gating doc.

marin: closing loop later this week with the RFC draft. :wave:
